A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMI-AW study and contain readable main text and complete supplementary material. Methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched reliably despite reference reflow and shifted appendix pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original inversion experiments on FaceScrub, CelebA and StanfordDogs, human evaluations in Table 4, and supplementary prompt-variation and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including quantitative results in Tables 1–4 and S.1–S.2 and qualitative reconstructions from fine-tuned and publicly released VLMs.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4, adaptive attention-based token weighting, and the three inversion-loss formulations in supplementary Section 4.1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FaceScrub, CelebA and StanfordDogs tasks, FFHQ and AFHQ-Dogs public data, and fine-tuned and publicly released VLM evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same TMI, TMI-C, SMI and SMI-AW comparisons, with identical loss variants within each experiment. Table S.2 also retains the same SMI versus SMI-AW comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and supplementary Sections 1 and 4 retain the same model configurations, data selection, 70 inversion steps, candidate-selection procedures, metrics and human-evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The prompt-variation ablation in Table S.1, match-rate analysis in Figure 3, attention analyses in Figures 2 and S.9–S.12, and qualitative reconstruction cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments in Table S.2 were repeated three times with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and S.1–S.2, plotted results and reconstruction examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 61.01% MLLM-evaluated attack accuracy on FaceScrub, and Table 4 retains 61.21% human-evaluated accuracy on CelebA for LLaVA-v1.6-7B.

T1.justification: The white-box problem formulation, mathematical definitions and Equations 1–8 are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: a first systematic study of VLM inversion, token- and sequence-based strategies, adaptive weighting, and vulnerability of fine-tuned and publicly released VLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual grounding and gradient informativeness remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 6.2 retains the same limitations concerning facial/dog-image coverage and the need for broader domains and additional models.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v2's statement that code and additional experiments are provided in the supplement with an explicit project-page link advertising code and models. This changes resource-access guidance; implementation details and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: The same 47 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to unimodal inversion research. Bibliographic differences are updated page back-references caused by pagination changes.

P1.justification: v3 adds a University of Maryland affiliation for Sy-Tuyen Ho and a funding-acknowledgements paragraph, rewrites the abstract's resource-availability sentence, and makes a small acronym edit. The scientific narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation line and revised abstract alter first-page layout, while the acknowledgements reflow the references onto an additional page. Figures, tables, captions and supplementary page layouts are otherwise unchanged apart from pagination and page references.

improvement.justification: Replacing the vague supplementary-code pointer with an explicit project-page link and code-and-models availability statement modestly improves resource discoverability and reproducibility guidance. The scientific content and evidence remain unchanged; actual accessibility and completeness of the linked resources cannot be established from the PDFs.
